programme.title: Moogly: Other Yarn Crafts
programme.desc: Let's explore some yarn crafts outside of crochet

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Turning Water Into Oil
programme.desc: I get quite a few questions about water-based finishes and how to make them look more like oil-based finishes. It’s a common problem since water-based finishes are “water-white,” which means they don’t impart any color to the wood and have the potential to leave the surface looking lifeless and boring. In this video, I show you three different ways to treat the wood surface so that even WITH a water-based topcoat, the wood looks more like an oil-based finish.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Sculpted End Table Part 5
programme.desc: I'll show you how I use a Kutzall carving burr and a die grinder to blend in the protruding center piece, and I discuss the creation of the template for the top. I also show you how I rout the grooves for the steel dowels that will suspend the tabletop in the middle of the piece (you’ll understand when you see it).

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: David Marks Project in Progress
programme.desc: This is a quick tour of David Marks project in progress. David loves to make massive turned sculptures and his current project is a doozie! It’s a huge disc-shaped turned piece featuring a big marquetry image on the front. I hope you enjoy this as much as I did. It’s almost like an episode of Woodworks! Well, sort of.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Sculpted End Table Part 2
programme.desc: I discuss sliding dovetails and show you how to make them. I also cover finessing the dovetail’s fit and some special techniques for creating a stopped sliding dovetails.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: 10 Things I Wish I Knew When I Started Woodworking
programme.desc: Some tips that might save you some heartache, time and money.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: River Bend Windsor Chair Kit
programme.desc: My friends at the Woodwerks Supply in Ohio sent me one of their new River Bend Windsor Chair Kits. This video outlines the process of putting this kit together and I even go so far as to give you a few compelling reasons why a kit like this makes sense for new AND experienced woodworkers alike!

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Dream Closet Build Part 1
programme.desc: Making my wife a dream closet to replace the builder grade wire shelving.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Classy Headphone Controller Rack
programme.desc: An elegant and simple rack that holes a game controller and a set of headphones.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Waterborne Finishes & HVLP
programme.desc: Technically, this is really Part 4 of our Wall-Hanging Tool Chest build, but because I focused so strongly on waterborne finishes and HVLP (High Volume Low Pressure spraying), it received its own stand-alone title.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Low Entertainment Center Part 1
programme.desc: Think you can’t build furniture because you only have a few basic tools? Well, check this out! This walnut low entertainment center was built using three primary tools: a circular saw, a router, and a drill. The unit has sliding doors, good ventilation, a little shelf in the back for a surge protector, and all of the trim is beveled at an angle for a more interesting visual effect

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: How to Create Pillowed Legs
programme.desc: Whenever I make legs for a table or chair, I find it difficult to leave them square and flat on each face. Ever since I saw David Marks pillow the outside faces of his Bubinga Coffee Table on WoodWorks, I always like to consider the possibility of using that technique to spice things up.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Flatten Boards Wider Than Your Jointer
programme.desc: I'm going to show you two techniques that will help you keep your wide boards intact. Both methods utilize the planer for final flattening, but one method starts with a hand plane and the other starts with the jointer.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Natural Wood Color Changes aka A Colorful Conversation
programme.desc: Learn with Marc about the science of natural wood color changes.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Gadget Station Part 12
programme.desc: Well I finally made it to the finish line. This episode covers the hinge installation, pegging the tenons in the doors, making custom ebony handles, and finishing. I end the video with a justification of my design.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Dining Chair
programme.desc: You might recall the Gaming Dining Table I built in season 9. Ever since then, Nicole has been asking repeatedly, "When do I get my chairs?" So I started designing a new chair that I'd eventually batch out for a total of six. The video I've assembled here is a quick look at the process of designing and building the chair.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Assembly of a PM2000 Table Saw
programme.desc: I have been running a PM2000 in my shop for nearly 10 years and the move to Colorado afforded me the opportunity to sell the old one and replace it with a newer version that features a 50″ fence and the heavier duty workbench extension. And I thought it would be a good time to show you how to assemble a Powermatic PM2000.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Outdoor Finishes - Real World Results
programme.desc: A look at how my outdoor projects have fared over the years.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Aging Wood with Baking Soda
programme.desc: While you are probably familiar with the pigment and dye-based stains available on the market, you might not be aware of a whole other class of stains known as chemical stains. Woods like mahogany and cherry are great candidates for chemical staining with baking soda but a wood like maple doesn't have much change, as you'll see in the video.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: SketchUp Basics - Trunk Lid Part 3
programme.desc: In the final part of our series, Aaron puts the finishing touches on the trunk lid. If this is your first experience with SketchUp, I highly recommend checking out the tutorials located at Sketch Up For Woodworkers

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Rocking Horse Part 2
programme.desc: The second and final video in this series covers finishing and assembly. As with any project, you should always ask yourself if it might be better to pre-finish the parts. Since the rocking horse would be incredibly difficult to finish after assembly and all of our parts are screwed together, pre-finishing was a no-brainer.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Knife Case and Box Joint Jig
programme.desc: Got knives? Here's a cool way to store and display them!

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Low Entertainment Center Part 2
programme.desc: If there is one major negative aspect to working with plywood and other sheetgoods, its the fact that we have to deal with the ugly exposed edges. But with a little know-how and some strips of wood, you can dress up the edges so that only a trained eye can tell that the board is not completely made of solid wood.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: So I Changed My Mind!
programme.desc: Over the years, I've changed my mind about finishes, workbench flatness, and some other things.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Shop Update - Tool Wall - Garage Door Cover - New Fans - DC Upgrades
programme.desc: Almost before I realized what was happening, I found myself fully engaged in phase 2 of my garage to shop conversion. 2x4s were purchased, nails were driven, and organization was born!

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Festool DF 500 Connectors
programme.desc: Like anything Festool, the system isn't cheap. But this Executive Desk is actually going to be my "lifetime" desk and build quality is a big priority, so I decided to give them a shot. The DF 500 Connectors have several configurations but I only needed one for my desk, and that's what I'll show you here.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Get Back Dining Table
programme.desc: The smartest, most durable, fun & useful space-saving table, built using white oak and the Swing-Out Seat Table Hardware Kit from Get Back Inc.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Tricking Out a Cheap Desk
programme.desc: Instead of replacing a cheap desk, let's see if we can trick it out and make it more functional.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: AWFS 2007 Special - Part 2 of 2
programme.desc: In this special, Marc visits AWFS to learn firsthand from manufacturers about their new and innovative products.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: New Festool Tools
programme.desc: Festool recently released two new routers, the MFK700 and the OF2200, and a new multi-function table, the MFT3. Judging from the emails I’ve received, there is a lot of interest in seeing these items on the show. So this one is for you guys!

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: The Taper Maker
programme.desc: Make your own tapering sled using our plans and hardware kit.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Guild to Woodworking Clamps aka The Big Squeeze
programme.desc: Not sure what woodworking clamps to buy? In this episode, Marc will answer all your questions and guide you to the best clamps!

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Craft Cart
programme.desc: A simple and functional craft cart that will help keep your kitchen table clean!

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Rustic Outdoor Table - Tops - Ends - Finish
programme.desc: The table top and bench tops come together along with the breadboard ends. Watco Teak Oil is used for the finish.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Festool CMS Router Table
programme.desc: Festool's new CMS Router Table hits the market in October 2012. Here's a first look at some of the main features and add-ons!

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Woodworking in America 2010
programme.desc: This was my first WIA and my expectations were building all year long. I even vowed to skip IWF (the big tool show in Atlanta), just to make sure I could focus all my attention on this education-focused conference. And am I ever glad I did!

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Repurposed Outdoor Coffee Table
programme.desc: An old table has a new life as a coffee table.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Gadget Station Part 11
programme.desc: I resaw the spalted maple panels on the bandsaw using Laguna’s Resaw King. What a bandsaw blade! I then glue up the doors and begin creating the ebony plugs for the case. I finish up by showing my process for fitting inset doors.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Setting Up a Dado Blade
programme.desc: A hassle-free method for setting up a dado blade with no measuring! All it takes is a flat surface and one of the most sensitive measuring devices in your shop: your fingers!

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Tool Storage Cabinet
programme.desc: Tool storage is a challenge for any workshop. My current dilemma is how to store my portable power tools so that they are out of their cases and accessible. There is no one-size-fits-all solution, but I hope sharing my thoughts on this topic will at least get your gears turning so you can tackle the storage challenges in your own shop.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: How to Refinish & Repurpose Cabinet Doors aka From Southwest to Contemporary
programme.desc: My mom's house is full of cabinet doors that were made in a Southwestern style and its time for a change. REPlacing the cabinets is certainly an option and just rEPlacing the doors alone would work too. But what if we could use our woodworking skills to modify the doors instead.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: 2018 Holiday Gift Guide
programme.desc: Our annual holiday gift guide with some of our favorite woodworking gifts.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Drawbored Mortise & Tenon
programme.desc: The mortise and tenon is one of the strongest fundamental joints available to woodworkers, but there are a couple of ways we can make the joint even stronger and longer-lasting.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Quick High-Quality Shop Cabinets
programme.desc: A new set of custom cabinets with oodles of storage!

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Drill Charging Station & DowelMax
programme.desc: I realized I needed a better way to store my drills and chargers. This simple wall-hanging “box” did the trick. I also wanted to make the project fast and easy, so I decided to try out the DowelMax for the first time. The system is a breeze to use and produces strong reliable joints in just a fraction of the time it takes to create a traditional mortise and tenon.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: In-Drawer Knife Block
programme.desc: A handy and safe way to organize kitchen knifes inside a drawer.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Build a Blanket Ladder
programme.desc: Nicole joins me for a new beginner series of projects starting with a handy blanket ladder.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Shop Safety - My Mistakes
programme.desc: In the years since I started woodworking, I have only had a few close calls. Fortunately, most of my injuries have been minor. Most of those injuries took place early in my career before I knew anything about anything. This video will show you some of the stupid mistakes I’ve made, what happened to me, and how I avoid repeating those mistakes.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: A Moving Experience
programme.desc: Moving an entire wood shop is no fun. But you can save yourself a lot of backaches if you hire some help. Money well-spent if you ask me. I'll show you everything I did to get my shop ready for the road trip. By no means is this meant to be a guide of any sort. Rather, its just a peek into my personal experience. And if you ever have to move your own shop, you’ll know what you’re in for.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Safety Week 2008
programme.desc: Woodworker’s Safety Week is finally here! No it doesn’t mean that this is the only week we have to be safe, haha. Obviously, our shops are full of danger. So its very important that we adopt the safest practices possible. And with so many folks new to the hobby, its critical that we take a step back occasionally and focus on safety.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Advent Calendar Part 1
programme.desc: This Advent calendar is relatively basic in design, but has 25 little cubbies with enough room for a special treat or a secret message. In the first part of the two-part series, I start working on the grid structure and the hanging of the doors. The grid structure is creating using a shop-made jig that is very similar to a box-joint jig.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: How to Make a Vacuum Bag aka A Pressing Matter
programme.desc: Marc teaches how to make your own vacuum bag for veneer press.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Finishing the Arts & Crafts Table
programme.desc: In this episode, Marc shows how to add a curve to the bottom rails and the sides of your arts & crafts table.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: SketchUp Basics - Trunk Lid Part 1
programme.desc: Its no secret that Google SketchUp is a very popular program amongst woodworkers. Considering what it does, its incredibly easy to use. But it can still be intimidating to someone who is using it for the first time. So with the help of my buddy Aaron Marshall, we put together a few videos showing how to construct the square lid to the Steamer Trunk.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: 4-In-A-Row Game
programme.desc: This 4-In-A-Row Game is fun for the whole family and can be made with basic materials and tools. If you're not familiar with this classic game, the goal is to achieve four discs in a row while blocking your competitor from doing the same. The fact that it's oversized makes it that much more fun.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Interview with Kaleo Kala
programme.desc: A chat with woodworker and designer, Kaleo Kala.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Bit Storage Cabinet
programme.desc: A wall-hanging cabinet to help you organize and store your drill and router bits.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Cool Miter Clamping Trick
programme.desc: A simple jig that will help you clamp large miter joints, such as those found in Mid-Century Modern furniture.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Backlit LED Poster Frame Light Box
programme.desc: Nicole and I love movies and we are lucky to have our own home theater room. Just outside that room, is a recess with an outlet on the wall intended for a back-lit poster frame. The one that came with the house was made with fluorescent tubes and was falling apart. So this is my replacement. It features a dimmable LED light strip and a double-sided poster and accEPts 27″ x 40″ posters.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: A Quick and Dirty 2lb Cut of Shellac
programme.desc: If you ever research mixing shellac, you were probably overwhelmed with information about precise measurements, including weights and volumes.
